decisions.title: Does a `require-confirmation` rider item block the advance freeze, and by what mechanism?
decisions.rule: A requirement flagged `require-confirmation` never resolves to `match` from listing data; it holds at `unknown`, basis `awaiting-confirmation`, until a named human at the venue confirms. The row then uses the EXISTING machinery: 18.03.01 source-1's `unknown` -> venue-side question, 18.03.01 D-06's 'an `unknown` on a hard requirement is `hard`', and 18.03.01 D-05/D-07's hard-outstanding freeze gate. No new generation source, no exception to D-04, no new severity branch.
decisions.precedent: 16.05.05 D-03 already forces `match` -> `unknown` on stale show-stopping rows (cited at 18.03.02:241). 18.04.01 DT-11's 'listing data is not consent' is the same claim about a different kind of untrustworthiness.

changes.edge_cases: Two new rows (3 columns each, matching the table): the satisfying-value case, and the shortfall case, which confirms the verification axis only ever blocks the path to `match` and never rescues a room that cannot meet the requirement.

untouched_as_ratified.why: A `match` still generates no item. The whole point of Option B is that a `require-confirmation` row is no longer a match, so D-04 needs no exception and no caveat. Verified by `git diff -U0 | grep '^[+-]| D-0'` over the file returning nothing.
'An `unknown` on a hard requirement is `hard`' already derives the severity. No new branch was added. Verified the same way.

Qualifier count still reads five — `basis`, `caveats[]`, `confidence`, `severity`, `judgement-required`. `basis` is an enum whose value list grew from seven to eight; that is not a sixth qualifier. Both prose restatements ('three outcomes, five qualifiers' at the section heading and 'Every row additionally carries five qualifiers') are also unchanged.
Three orthogonal flags stand. Only the `verification` axis's consumer and effect were restated, in the flag table, the Happy Path, the edge cases, the cross-cut notes and new D-13.
'capability != availability != consent' is the argument D-17 implements, not one it displaces. New D-13's context says so explicitly.

open_questions_left.note: Two halves the ratified statement does not license an answer to. (1) Harvest: D-17's rows clear on a human answer, but that answer is a CONSENT ('you may use the Steinway on the 14th'), not a CAPABILITY STATEMENT ('we have a Steinway'), and DT-12's harvest re-verifies 16 fields from advance answers — routing a consent into 16.05.05 as a field verification would launder a one-night permission into a standing property of the room, the mirror image of the laundering 18.03.01 DT-14 rejects. (2) Persistence: does March's confirmation carry to October's date, or does every date ask again? 18.03.03's per-date overlay says compromises never carry; whether consent behaves the same way is stated nowhere. Both are field-provenance semantics owned across 16.05.03/16.05.05 and 18.03.02, so 18 cannot close them alone — which is also why nothing was written into domain 16.
